content.summary: This interview evaluates a candidate’s grasp of core networking fundamentals required for entry‑level or junior networking roles. It probes conceptual depth (OSI/TCP‑IP models, addressing, routing, switching, DNS, security), practical problem‑solving (subnet calculations, protocol troubleshooting), and the ability to communicate technical ideas clearly—mirroring real‑world networking tasks and interview expectations.

competencies.name: OSI Model Mastery
competencies.description: Deep understanding of the 7‑layer OSI model and ability to map protocols and services to the correct layers

competencies.name: TCP/IP Stack Proficiency
competencies.description: Knowledge of the TCP, IP, UDP, ICMP protocols, their headers, and interaction across layers

competencies.name: IP Addressing & Subnetting
competencies.description: Ability to calculate subnets, CIDR notation, VLSM, and perform binary conversions quickly

competencies.name: Routing Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understanding of static routing, distance‑vector and link‑state protocols, and route selection criteria

competencies.name: Switching & VLANs
competencies.description: Knowledge of Ethernet switching, MAC learning, trunking, VLAN design, and inter‑VLAN routing

competencies.name: DNS & DHCP Operations
competencies.description: Comprehension of name resolution, zone types, DHCP lease process, and common troubleshooting steps

competencies.name: Network Security Basics
competencies.description: Familiarity with firewalls, ACLs, VPN types, NAT, and basic hardening practices

competencies.name: Performance & QoS Concepts
competencies.description: Understanding of latency, jitter, throughput, and QoS mechanisms like shaping and policing

competencies.name: Wireless Networking Fundamentals
competencies.description: Basic concepts of Wi‑Fi standards, SSID, encryption, and site‑survey considerations

question_areas.guidance: Explain each layer, typical protocols, and why layering matters; map real‑world examples to layers
Describe the role of TCP vs UDP, header fields, and how IP fragmentation/reassembly works
Perform subnet calculations, explain CIDR, and discuss why subnetting improves network efficiency
Compare distance‑vector vs link‑state, describe convergence, and outline when to use static routes
Explain MAC learning, broadcast domains, VLAN tagging (802.1Q), and trunking concepts
Detail the DNS query process, zone delegation, DHCP lease cycle, and common failure points
Discuss firewall rule ordering, NAT types, VPN tunnel basics, and basic hardening steps
Define latency, jitter, throughput; illustrate how QoS policies prioritize traffic
Cover Wi‑Fi standards (802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax), encryption methods, and interference mitigation
Introduce VPCs, subnets, security groups, and basic concepts of hybrid connectivity

preparation_plan: Read and summarise the OSI and TCP/IP models, noting key protocols per layer
Complete subnetting exercises covering /30 to /16 ranges and practice CIDR calculations
Watch tutorials on routing (RIP, OSPF, BGP) and set up basic routes in a lab environment (e.g., GNS3 or Packet Tracer)
Configure VLANs and inter‑VLAN routing on a switch/router simulator to reinforce switching concepts
Review DNS, DHCP, and NAT operations; set up a small virtual network to observe these services in action
Study common network security mechanisms (firewalls, ACLs, VPNs) and their placement within the OSI model
Read articles on QoS, latency, and throughput; calculate sample bandwidth scenarios
Practice explaining networking concepts aloud to improve clarity and storytelling
